market_context: The Nasdaq-100 fell 2.67% to 27,197.15 (QQQ −2.67% to $661.75) in a third straight decline, as chip and AI stocks sold off ahead of Nvidia’s Tuesday earnings; the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 5.28%. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called over the weekend for a “dramatic shakeup” at Nvidia, and the Commerce Department issued new rules tightening overseas access to advanced AI chips.
market_cap_basis: Shares outstanding x 2026-11-16 close. Shares implied from Nasdaq market caps as of the 2026-10-29 close (watchlist market_cap_usd / 2026-10-29 close), so multi-class companies (e.g. GOOGL) reflect all share classes.

stocks.name: Arm Holdings plc American Depositary Shares
stocks.reason: Arm fell with the semiconductor sector ahead of Nvidia earnings. Motley Fool reported that research firm SemiAnalysis issued a weekend update to institutional clients cutting AI-accelerator revenue estimates by 19% to 41% for 2027–2030; Arm’s licensing ties to Nvidia, a rich valuation, and lingering speculation that CEO Rene Haas could be a candidate for Nvidia’s job left the stock more exposed.
